subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Baba Budan: The Sacred Smuggler
description: A quick win: understand Baba Budan: The Sacred Smuggler.

hook.text: In the 1600s, a Sufi pilgrim named Baba Budan smuggled seven coffee beans out of Yemen—strapped to his belly.

buildup.text: Yemen jealously guarded its coffee monopoly. Exporting fertile beans was forbidden; only roasted (dead) seeds could leave.

discovery.text: Baba Budan planted his seven beans in the hills of southern India. They thrived. India became a coffee-growing nation.

twist.text: The hills where he planted are still called 'Baba Budan Giri' today. They remain one of India's premier coffee regions.

climax.text: His seven beans ended Yemen's monopoly. Every coffee plant outside Arabia and Ethiopia may trace to similar smuggling.

punchline.text: Seven beans, one belly, a broken monopoly. Coffee's spread was an act of holy theft.

quiz.question: Why did Baba Budan have to smuggle coffee beans out of Yemen?
options: Yemen forbade exporting fertile beans to protect its monopoly
